concepts.name: Inflation and Redistribution of Income & Wealth
key_dimensions: Debtors vs. creditors: who gains and who loses during inflation
Fixed-income earners (pensioners, wage workers) vs. asset holders (real estate, equity owners)
Regressive nature of inflation as an implicit tax on the poor
UPSC trap: Inflation benefits debtors but harms creditors — distinguishing nominal vs. real debt burden

concepts.name: Inflation Tax and Seigniorage
key_dimensions: Definition: government revenue from money printing that erodes purchasing power of currency holders
Seigniorage as a source of fiscal financing in developing economies
Relationship between hyperinflation and excessive money supply growth (Quantity Theory linkage)
UPSC trap: Inflation tax is NOT a formal tax — it is an implicit levy; distinguishing it from regular taxation

concepts.name: Effect of Inflation on Savings and Capital Formation
key_dimensions: Negative real interest rates discouraging financial savings (bank deposits)
Shift from financial savings to physical savings (gold, real estate) — 'financialization vs. physicalization'
Impact on long-term capital formation and investment rates in the economy
UPSC trap: High inflation can INCREASE nominal savings but DECREASE real savings — the nominal vs. real distinction

concepts.name: Inflation and Investment Climate (Business Uncertainty)
key_dimensions: Price uncertainty increasing the risk premium demanded by investors
Shortening of investment horizons — preference for short-term over long-term projects
Effect on FDI inflows: high inflation as a signal of macroeconomic instability
UPSC trap: Mild inflation can stimulate investment (profit expectation), but high/volatile inflation deters it — the non-linear relationship

concepts.name: Phillips Curve: Inflation–Unemployment Trade-off
key_dimensions: Original short-run Phillips Curve: inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment
Long-run Phillips Curve: vertical at NAIRU — no permanent trade-off
Stagflation of the 1970s as empirical refutation of the simple Phillips Curve
UPSC trap: The trade-off exists only in the SHORT RUN; confusing short-run and long-run versions is a classic trap

concepts.name: Inflation and Real Wages vs. Nominal Wages
key_dimensions: Distinction between nominal wage increase and real wage erosion during inflation
Money illusion: workers may not immediately perceive real wage cuts — implications for labor markets
Wage-price spiral: how persistent inflation feeds into wage demands and further price rises
UPSC trap: A nominal wage rise during inflation does NOT mean workers are better off — real wage must be computed

concepts.name: Effects of Inflation on Government Finances (Fiscal Effects)
key_dimensions: Erosion of real value of government debt (beneficial to the government as a debtor)
Bracket creep (fiscal drag): inflation pushing taxpayers into higher tax brackets without real income gains
Inflation boosting nominal tax revenues (GST, income tax) — improving fiscal deficit optics
UPSC trap: Inflation can simultaneously help government (debt erosion, higher revenues) AND hurt it (higher subsidy bill, interest payments on indexed bonds)

concepts.name: Inflation and External Sector: Trade Competitiveness and Current Account
key_dimensions: Domestic inflation making exports costlier and imports cheaper — deterioration of trade balance
Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) theory: inflation differential driving exchange rate depreciation
How RBI's inflation management is linked to exchange rate stability and BoP health
UPSC trap: Inflation leads to currency depreciation (not appreciation) — confusing cause and effect in PPP

concepts.name: Inflation and Exchange Rate: Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
key_dimensions: Absolute PPP vs. Relative PPP — which is more relevant for inflation analysis
Higher domestic inflation → depreciation of domestic currency under PPP
Limitations of PPP: non-tradable goods, trade barriers, Balassa-Samuelson effect
UPSC trap: PPP holds better in LONG RUN — short-run exchange rates are driven by capital flows, speculation

concepts.name: Hyperinflation: Causes, Consequences, and Historical Cases
key_dimensions: Defining hyperinflation (Cagan's definition: >50% per month) vs. galloping inflation
Case studies: Weimar Germany (1923), Zimbabwe (2008) — causes (war financing, political instability, money printing)
Economic collapse: breakdown of price signals, barter economy revival, dollarization
UPSC trap: Hyperinflation is a monetary phenomenon but triggered by FISCAL collapse — the fiscal-monetary nexus

concepts.name: Stagflation: Inflation with Stagnation
key_dimensions: Definition: simultaneous occurrence of high inflation, high unemployment, and low growth
Supply-side causes: oil price shocks (1973 OPEC crisis) as a classic example
Policy dilemma: conventional tools (tightening) cure inflation but worsen unemployment
UPSC trap: Stagflation CANNOT be addressed by standard demand management — supply-side reforms are needed; often confused with recession

concepts.name: Deflation and Deflationary Spiral: Opposite but Equally Harmful
key_dimensions: Why deflation is harmful: postponement of consumption, rising real debt burden, liquidity trap
Debt-deflation spiral (Irving Fisher): falling prices → higher real debt → defaults → further deflation
Japan's 'Lost Decade' as a case study of deflationary stagnation
UPSC trap: Deflation appears beneficial (prices falling) but is economically dangerous — the paradox of thrift connection

concepts.name: Core Inflation vs. Headline Inflation: Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Headline inflation includes food and fuel; Core inflation excludes these volatile components
Why RBI focuses on headline CPI for inflation targeting but monitors core for underlying demand pressure
Sticky core inflation as a greater policy concern than volatile headline inflation
UPSC trap: India's inflation targeting framework targets HEADLINE CPI (not core) — a frequently tested factual distinction

concepts.name: Asset Price Inflation vs. Consumer Price Inflation
key_dimensions: Asset price inflation (stocks, real estate) not captured in CPI/WPI baskets
Wealth inequality amplification: asset inflation benefits the wealthy disproportionately
Role of easy monetary policy (low interest rates, QE) in fueling asset bubbles
UPSC trap: Central banks traditionally target CPI, NOT asset prices — debate on whether monetary policy should 'lean against the wind' of asset bubbles

concepts.name: Inflation Expectations and Credibility of Monetary Policy
key_dimensions: Rational expectations theory: if people expect inflation, it becomes self-fulfilling
Role of central bank credibility (inflation targeting framework, MPC) in anchoring expectations
Forward guidance as a tool to manage inflation expectations without changing interest rates
UPSC trap: Expectations are a CAUSE of inflation, not just a consequence — the adaptive vs. rational expectations distinction

concepts.name: Inflation and Poverty: Distributional Impact on Vulnerable Sections
key_dimensions: Food inflation disproportionately hurts the poor (higher share of food in consumption basket of poor)
Erosion of real value of social transfers, MGNREGA wages, and MSP if not indexed to inflation
Inflation as a barrier to poverty alleviation and human development outcomes
UPSC trap: CPI (Rural) and CPI (Urban) differ — rural poor face higher food inflation impact; WPI is NOT a measure of consumer burden

concepts.name: Optimal Inflation Rate: Why Zero Inflation is Not the Target
key_dimensions: Zero inflation risks tipping into deflation — a small positive buffer is preferred (RBI target: 4%)
Greasing the wheels hypothesis: mild inflation facilitates real wage adjustment without nominal cuts
Measurement bias in price indices (CPI overstates true inflation) — justifying a positive target
UPSC trap: The ideal inflation target is NOT zero — understanding the rationale behind India's 4% (+/-2%) target under FRBM/MPC framework

concepts.name: Sectoral Effects of Inflation: Agriculture, Industry, and Services
key_dimensions: Farmers as net gainers from food inflation (seller of produce) vs. landless laborers as losers
Input cost inflation (raw materials, fuel) squeezing industrial profit margins — cost-push dynamics
Services sector: wages are major cost — wage inflation feeding into services price inflation
UPSC trap: Farmers are NOT always beneficiaries of food inflation — net-buyer farmers (small/marginal) LOSE; the distinction between net-buyer and net-seller farmers

concepts.name: Inflation and Financial Sector Stability
key_dimensions: High inflation eroding real returns on fixed-income instruments (bonds, FDs) — financial repression
Interest rate volatility from inflation shocks creating mark-to-market losses for banks (bond portfolio risk)
Inflation-indexed bonds (IIBs) as instruments to protect investors — RBI's role in issuing them
UPSC trap: Rising inflation leads RBI to HIKE rates → bond prices FALL → banks holding bonds face losses — the inverse bond price-yield relationship is frequently tested

concepts.name: Imported Inflation and Global Commodity Price Transmission
key_dimensions: How global crude oil, edible oil, and fertilizer price shocks transmit into domestic inflation
Role of exchange rate depreciation in amplifying imported inflation (currency pass-through effect)
India's vulnerability: high import dependence on crude oil, vegetable oils, fertilizers
UPSC trap: RBI's monetary policy has LIMITED effectiveness against IMPORTED inflation (supply-side/external) — the instrument mismatch problem
